findings.note: DESK #155 (owner 2026-09-12, from the live Archives page): a spellbook caster — wizard, witch via the familiar, magus — who takes Flexible Spellcaster KEEPS the book and the curriculum/restricted slots and prepares the flat collection OUT OF THE BOOK. The ENGINE half is CODE and shipped with this round: src/rules/build.ts extracts `fillSpellCollection` (Table 5-1's flat pool, the 1st-rank floor, the capstone carve-out) out of the collection branch so the BOOK branch calls it with the assembled spellbook once `archSpellMods.spellCollection` is set, and stops building the per-slot `prepared`; src/builder/Builder.tsx reads the CLASS's own casting type for `isWizardBook` (the archetype flips `castType` to spontaneous, which had been taking the book away from every flexible wizard/witch/magus and offering a 4-place "collection" where the book holds eleven) and keeps `isFlexCollection` off a book caster's rail; src/sheet/SpellsTab.tsx offers the BOOK to a spontaneous entry that has one, so the collection can no longer be stocked from the whole tradition. Pinned by test/desk155-flexible-book-casters.test.tsx. NO NEW FIELD carries any of it: the pool size is still derived from the character's own capped slot table (a stored number would be a second copy of Table 5-1, the reason batch 037 refused one), and the cantrip ladder is already encoded — spellSlotBonus.cantrips 1 + cantripsAt level 4 → 2, composed with classArchetype.cantripDelta −2, which measures 4 at 2nd and 5 at 4th on a five-cantrip class and one higher on a wizard, whose sixth class cantrip is the school's. The single row below is the PLAYER-FACING half: the class-archetype note the sheet prints (src/sheet/FeatsTab.tsx:387) told the player the collection is one flat pool with a 1st-rank floor and that restricted slots are untouched, but never said WHERE the collection's spells come from — which is the whole of desk #155 and the only sentence a wizard, witch or magus needs that a cleric does not.

backfillRows.value: Flexible Spellcaster: you prepare a spell COLLECTION rather than filling each slot, and can cast any spell in it using any slot of an appropriate rank. The collection is ONE pool, not a list per rank: it holds as many spells as the total spell slots you get each day from your class, in any mix of ranks, and at least one of them must be 1st rank. That total counts your 1st- to 9th-rank slots only: a single 10th-rank slot from a class feature stays OUTSIDE the collection and works just as it always did, so the spell you choose for it is not one of the collection's spells and does not use up one of its places. You learn spells as normal for your class and select the collection from that same source — a wizard or magus still learns a spellbook and prepares the collection out of it, a witch still teaches spells to their familiar — so nothing changes about how you get spells, only how you prepare them. In exchange your slots per rank never advance past 2, and you learn 2 fewer class cantrips. Restricted slots (a wizard curriculum slot, a cleric divine font) are unaffected and their spells do not count toward the collection.
backfillRows.why: AoN archetype-99 (Secrets of Magic pg. 209): "You learn spells as normal for your class (a wizard uses a spellbook, a witch teaches spells to their familiar, and so on), but you prepare them differently" and "Select these spells from the same source as normal, such as from a spellbook for a wizard." The shipped note named the pool's size, its 1st-rank floor, the capstone carve-out and the restricted-slot exemption but never its SOURCE, so a wizard, witch or magus reading their own sheet was told they now hold a collection and not told it comes out of the book they still keep — the one sentence desk #155 is about. The cantrip half of the same feat (feat-2994, "four cantrips per day instead of three. At 4th level, five instead of four") is already carried by this record's spellSlotBonus ladder and needs no row. Owner ruling 2026-09-12, desk #155.
